comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that ants use lunar polarisation for navigation (C1, C9, C10, C42-C48, C83). Peer review emphasizes this as 'first proof' with 'very clear' and 'unambiguous' data. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation (p<0.001 to p<0.01) and notes bidirectional response patterns. Peer review additionally addresses novelty claims (C81-C82) and nest differences (C50-C52) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Both support detection across lunar phases (C11, C53-C59, C63, C84, C116). OpenEval notes increased variability in crescent moon conditions but concludes this doesn't undermine the finding. Peer review confirms results are 'maintained even for different phases (and intensities)' without raising concerns. Both treat the cross-phase detection as clearly demonstrated.

Perfect claim overlap (C60-C62, C121) on No Moon control conditions. Both evaluations support this as critical negative control evidence. OpenEval emphasizes it rules out alternative explanations (stored solar compass, non-specific responses). Peer review implicitly accepts it as part of well-designed experiments without detailed discussion.

Perfect claim overlap (C64-C74, C86, C122-C124, C126-C128) on waxing/waning differences. Both support the finding that waning phases show reduced heading shifts. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis and notes the mechanistic interpretation is reasonable but not fully exclusive. Peer review treats this as clear behavioral data showing cue gaps affect navigation.

Strong overlap (C75-C80, C89-C90, C105-C106, C109) on vector-dependent cue weighting. Both strongly support this finding. OpenEval emphasizes the elegant experimental design dissociating vector length from spatial location with strong statistical evidence (p<0.001). Peer review explicitly confirms this parallels solar polarisation patterns and demonstrates integration into path integration.

OpenEval addresses nest differences (C50-C52) as separate result, finding it statistically significant but somewhat confounded by distance and vector length varying together. Peer review includes these claims within broader evaluation of core findings but doesn't specifically discuss the nest comparison or its limitations.

High overlap (C91-C92, C98-C101, C110-C112, C134) on comparison with solar polarisation. Both support the behavioral parallels between lunar and solar polarisation use. OpenEval notes quantitative similarity but cautions that shared neural pathway inference is speculative without neurophysiological evidence. Peer review treats the parallel as strengthening the interpretation without raising concerns about mechanistic claims.

OpenEval separately evaluates novelty claims (C81-C82) as supported, noting distinction from dung beetle straight-line maintenance. Peer review addresses same background context (C25-C29 in R7) confirming this is first evidence for homing use, treating novelty as clearly established.

OpenEval's novelty evaluation (C81-C82) relates to peer review's discussion of prior dung beetle work (C25-C29). Both confirm this is the first demonstration of lunar polarisation use for goal-directed homing versus straight-line trajectory maintenance. The evaluations align on the novelty claim being well-supported.

OpenEval rates observation about filter exit delays (C102-C103) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantitative data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. This represents a potential measurement error source that OpenEval identifies but peer reviewers did not explicitly address.

Minimal overlap (C107-C108) on multi-cue integration inference. OpenEval supports this based on vector-length experiments showing state-dependent weighting. Peer review addresses overlapping vector-dependent findings (C75-C80, C89-C90, C105-C106) but doesn't separately evaluate the multi-cue integration interpretation that OpenEval highlights.

Minimal overlap (C117) on maintained detection across phases. OpenEval supports the inference while noting limitations in distinguishing physiological from behavioral factors. Peer review confirms detection is maintained across phases (C117 included with C11, C53-C59, C63, C84, C116) without discussing the mechanistic ambiguity OpenEval raises.

OpenEval rates speculation about lunar ephemeris mechanisms (C129-C132) as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting these are open questions not resolved by current experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. Peer reviewers did not explicitly address these speculative mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims (C2-C6, C13-C23) about polarisation physics and moonlight properties as SUPPORTED by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These are standard background claims that peer reviewers implicitly accept but don't explicitly evaluate.

OpenEval evaluates methodological claims (C138-C146) as SUPPORTED with appropriate detail for replication. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers describe experiments as 'very well designed' and 'conducted carefully' without evaluating specific methodological claims.
